methodology: The study utilized surface-initiated RAFT (O2-SI-RAFT) polymerization under ambient conditions to grow polymer brushes on magnetic nanoparticles. The process involved the use of a charged monomer and a chiral monomer, with oxygen as the initiator for the polymerization reaction.
research_objective: To prepare and characterize magnetic nanoparticles grafted with functional polymers using surface-initiated RAFT polymerization under ambient conditions, thereby exploring the potential applications of these modified MNPs in various fields such as bio-separation, drug delivery, and biosensing.

key_findings.finding: Chiral polymers grown from MNPs have mirror images, confirming the ability to confer chiral properties on MNPs via O2-SI-RAFT polymerization.
O2-SI-RAFT polymerization was used to grow polymer brushes on Fe3O4@SiO2 MNPs, allowing for easy purification and chiral synthesis.
The polymerization of SPMA on Fe3O4@SiO2 MNPs via O2-SI-RAFT polymerization allowed for the successful grafting of CTA and subsequent growth of SPMA polymer brushes.
Fe3O4@SiO2@CTA@PSPMA MNPs retained their broad absorption peak at 470 nm, indicating the successful grafting of CTA and polymer brushes.
Successful creation of a core-shell structure with Fe3O4@SiO2 particles.
Polymer brushes (CTA and PSPMA) successfully grafted onto the Fe3O4@SiO2 nanoparticles, as evidenced by EDS mapping results.

properties.context: after RAFT-CTA coating and PSPMA polymer brush grafting

properties.property_name: elemental composition analysis by energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy (EDX)
properties.context: characterization using EDX for elemental analysis

properties.value: diameter of Fe3O4 particles: 200-230 nm, thickness of SiO2 protective group: ca. 16 nm
